issues.legal_issue: A tenant who has accepted a person as landlord by paying rent to that person cannot deny the landlord-tenant relationship with that person in a later eviction proceeding.
material_facts: The tenants accepted the original owner’s direction to pay rent to the rent recipient and paid rent to her.
The tenants later disputed her status as their landlord and the title derived from her.
issues.conclusion: The tenants were estopped from disputing the landlord-tenant relationship with the person to whom they had attorned.
issues.legal_principle: The Court applied estoppel based on the tenants’ own attornment and payment of rent. It cited no specific statutory provision or earlier case for this holding.

predicates.tenancy_eviction_case: The proceeding was brought to evict a tenant from leased premises.
predicates.tenant_attorned_to_rent_recipient: The tenant accepted a direction to treat a person as the landlord.
predicates.tenant_paid_rent_to_rent_recipient: The tenant paid rent to that person after accepting the direction.

issues.definition: When an eviction case follows the tenant’s acceptance of a person as landlord and payment of rent to that person, the tenant cannot deny that prior landlord relationship.

issues.legal_issue: A tenant cannot defeat a transferee landlord’s title in an eviction proceeding by alleging irregularities in an earlier public auction when the tenant has not proved the irregularities or obtained an order setting the auction sale aside.
material_facts: The property was sold at public auction to the rent recipient following a municipal tax recovery process, and the sale was confirmed.
The rent recipient later transferred the property to the landlord who brought the eviction proceedings.
The tenants alleged that the auction sale was fraudulent and procedurally invalid, but did not prove those allegations or show that the sale had been set aside.
The tenants did not bring a separate suit seeking a declaration that the auction sale was invalid.
issues.conclusion: The auction sale remained valid, the purchaser acquired title, and the subsequent transfer to the landlord was valid; the tenants could not challenge the auction sale in these eviction proceedings.
issues.legal_principle: The burden was on the tenants to prove that the sale was collusive, fraudulent, or conducted without required formalities. Until the sale is set aside, it remains effective. The Court stated that the tenants could challenge it by a separate suit for a declaration, which they had not brought.

rule.if: tenancy_eviction_case and property_acquired_at_public_auction and tenant_alleges_auction_irregularity and alleged_irregularity_unproved and auction_sale_not_set_aside

predicates.tenancy_eviction_case: The proceeding was brought to evict a tenant from leased premises.
predicates.property_acquired_at_public_auction: A predecessor in the landlord’s title acquired the property through a public auction.
predicates.tenant_alleges_auction_irregularity: The tenant alleged that the public auction was fraudulent or procedurally irregular.
predicates.alleged_irregularity_unproved: The tenant presented no proof that the alleged fraud or procedural irregularity occurred.
predicates.auction_sale_not_set_aside: No competent authority or court had set aside the auction sale.

issues.definition: In an eviction case, where a predecessor acquired the property at public auction and the tenant’s unproved challenge has not resulted in the sale being set aside, the transferee’s title is recognized.

issues.legal_issue: A property cannot be treated as evacuee property, and therefore immune from attachment and sale for municipal tax arrears, when that status has neither been pleaded nor proved.
material_facts: The tenants argued that the original owner’s migration meant the property had become evacuee property and could not be attached or sold.
The tenants raised that argument for the first time before the Supreme Court.
There was no pleading or proof that the property had been declared evacuee property.
issues.conclusion: The Court would not hold that the property was evacuee property or that it could not be attached and sold for municipal tax arrears.
issues.legal_principle: The Court required a factual basis, through pleadings and proof, for the claim that the property had acquired evacuee status; it cited no specific statutory provision or earlier case on this point.

rule.if: tenancy_eviction_case and tenant_claims_evacuee_status and evacuee_status_not_p pleaded and evacuee_status_not_proved

predicates.tenancy_eviction_case: The proceeding was brought to evict a tenant from leased premises.
predicates.tenant_claims_evacuee_status: The tenant asserted that the property had become evacuee property.
predicates.evacuee_status_not_p pleaded: The tenant did not plead that the property had been declared or otherwise acquired evacuee status.
predicates.evacuee_status_not_proved: The tenant offered no evidence establishing evacuee status.

issues.definition: In an eviction case, an unsupported claim of evacuee status does not result in the property being treated as evacuee property.

issues.legal_issue: A transferee landlord may recover pre-transfer rent as rent and rely on that arrearage in seeking eviction when the right to recover the arrears was assigned to the transferee.
material_facts: The predecessor landlord’s communication to the tenants stated that the property and arrears of rent were transferred to the new landlord and directed the tenants to pay the arrears to him.
The new landlord’s notice likewise claimed the pre-transfer rent arrears, and the tenants did not comply.
The tenants had not disputed in their pleadings that the predecessor assigned the right to recover the arrears.
The first appellate court found that the transferee was entitled to recover the pre-transfer arrears, and the Supreme Court inferred an assignment from the communications and that finding.
Including the assigned arrears, the tenants were in default for longer than the period required for eviction under the applicable rent law.
issues.conclusion: Because the right to recover the pre-transfer arrears had been assigned, the transferee could recover them as rent and seek eviction on the ground of default; the tenants’ arrears exceeded the statutory threshold, so the eviction order stood.
issues.legal_principle: Under Section 109 of the Transfer of Property Act, 1882, the transferee is ordinarily not entitled to pre-transfer rent arrears unless the right to recover them is assigned. If assigned, the arrears retain their character as rent and can support eviction under the applicable rent law. The Court relied on Satti Krishna Reddy v. Nallamilli Venkata Reddy, which rejected the contrary view in Smt. Daya Debi v. Chapla Debi; it also relied on Girdharilal v. Hukam Singh and N.M. Engineer v. Narendera Singh Virdi. It noted Ramchander Narsey & Co. v. Wamanrao Shenoy and held the single-judge view in Vinayak Mahadeo Nirgum v. Savannas Sanitarium Bandekar inconsistent with the applicable principles. Under the Bombay Rents, Hotel and Lodging House Rates Control Act, 1947, default exceeding six months on the date the suit is filed permits eviction on that ground.

rule.if: rent_control_eviction_case and arrears_assigned_to_transferee and assigned_rent_remains_unpaid and arrears_exceed_applicable_eviction_threshold

predicates.rent_control_eviction_case: The proceeding seeks a tenant’s eviction under rent-control law on the ground of non-payment of rent.
predicates.arrears_assigned_to_transferee: The predecessor landlord transferred to the new landlord the right to recover rent arrears that accrued before the transfer.
predicates.assigned_rent_remains_unpaid: The tenant did not pay the assigned rent arrears after the transferee sought payment.
predicates.arrears_exceed_applicable_eviction_thres: The unpaid rent arrears exceed the period of default required to support eviction under the applicable rent law.

issues.definition: When a rent-control eviction case involves unpaid pre-transfer arrears whose recovery right was assigned to the transferee, and the arrears exceed the applicable eviction threshold, the transferee may seek eviction based on those arrears.
